narrative:
The model determined that you have an 84% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The decision was driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was the status of your checking account, which is currently in negative balance. This is relatively uncommon—only 12.6% of approved applicants show a negative balance, while most maintain either no account or positive funds. This factor strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The second most important element was the requested loan duration of 60 months. This is more than three times longer than the average duration of about 19 months among those who were approved, and it significantly increased the model's assessment of risk.

Third, your lack of any recorded property ownership also contributed to the negative outcome. This situation is fairly rare among successful applicants and further tilted the prediction away from approval.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model viewed as carrying substantially higher risk than the typical approved borrower. 

To improve your chances in the future, focus on clearing your checking account into positive territory, reducing the amount or length of credit you request, and building verifiable assets or collateral. Addressing these areas should meaningfully strengthen future applications. (218 words)
